newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian Feb palm oil output seen down 10-15 pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian Feb palm oil output seen down 10-15 pct.

text.p: Malaysian palm oil output in February was estimated to have fallen between 10 and 15 percent over January, plantation houses said on Thursday.
The Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA), which is due to release official February crop data on March 15, put production in January at 576,967 tonnes.
"February output could have fallen more if not for the speedy recovery in the last half of the month," said an official at a plantation house.
"More fruits were harvested as workers returned from the long festive holiday (in early February)," he said.
The market had earlier expected a drop of up to 25 percent in February output.
Private forecaster Ivan Wong, in his last crop report, estimated February production at 502,000 tonnes, a 13 percent fall from January.
Traders have estimated end-February stocks at between 670,000 to 690,000 tonnes against end-January's 696,272 tonnes.
Exports in February were estimated at between 440,000-460,000 tonnes against 551,665 tonnes in January.
